extracted.intended_audience: high-school English students (Shepard Sophomore Academy, English 10H)
extracted.subtask_description: Create and perform a 3–5 minute partnered mock television editorial newscast that uses satiric techniques (in the manner of Jonathan Swift) to address a contemporary social issue. The project includes prewriting, a one- to two-page broadcast-formatted script, PowerPoint visuals, rehearsal, and an in-class presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of social issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and define a current social issue and who is affected by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewriting: Working with your partner brainstorm several contemporary social issues, who is affected by them, and what needs to be done to address each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency of issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an issue that is relatively current and newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Daily Show, The Colbert Report, and 'Weekend Update' base their satire upon recent events, generally news stories from the week prior. Your issue may extend past the week prior, but try to keep it relatively current. Your issue may be drawn from school, the city, the state, the nation, or the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitate established mock newscast form
rubrics_metrics.description: Model the piece on a short-form television satire segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can model your television script on a segment of Saturday Night Live's 'Weekend Update,' The Daily Show with Jon Stewart, or The Colbert Report. Your goal is to imitate the form of the mock newscast, which occurs at the beginning of The Daily Show and The Colbert Report; 'Weekend Update' occurs 30 minutes into SNL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outrageousness of solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose an absolutely outrageous solution to the problem in the manner of Swift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewriting: In the manner of Swift, propose an absolutely outrageous solution to address the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the outrageous solution would be implemented in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewriting: Determine how the solution would be implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsements of solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify persons (real or fictional) who might endorse the proposed solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewriting: What persons, either real or fictional, might endorse your solution?

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential objections and addressing them
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate potential objections to the proposal and plan concessions and refutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewriting: What potential objections might you encounter (both those that you might concede and those that you would refute)?

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of closing
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a suitable and effective closing for the proposal/newscast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewriting: Develop an appropriate closing for your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of satiric techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ satiric devices (e.g., verbal irony) to ridicule behaviors or institutions and push for social reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire is a literary technique in which people’s behaviors or society’s institutions are ridiculed for the purpose of bringing about social reform. One of the satirist’s most reliable tools is verbal irony, in which what is said is the opposite of what is meant. As you read 'A Modest Proposal,' notice how Swift uses verbal irony to present his seemingly rational proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format script for television broadcast
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the written address/script in broadcast format appropriate to a TV newscast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing: First, write the address for your newscaster to read to the 'television' audience (only a page or two long). Format your script for a television broadcast, being sure that both partners have equal participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script length (written)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the written script concise: approximately one to two pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing: First, write the address for your newscaster to read to the 'television' audience (only a page or two long).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the live presentation fits within the 3–5 minute time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice your presentation with your PowerPoint presentation so that it fits within a three- to five-minute broadcast segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal partner participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Both partners must participate equally in the script and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing: Format your script for a television broadcast, being sure that both partners have equal participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual/audio/video media
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and integrate images, audio tracks, or video to enhance satiric effects; use a PowerPoint as background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing / Revising / Editing: Brainstorm what sorts of images, audio tracks, or videos you might select to enhance the satiric effects of your newscast. Locate and download your desired images, audio, or video to use when preparing a PowerPoint presentation (not a Prezi) to provide the background images for your mock broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerPoint requirement (not Prezi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PowerPoint for background images; do not use Prezi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing: Prepare a PowerPoint presentation (not a Prezi) to provide the background images for your mock broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of visual images (evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual images chosen should be appropriate and enhance the satiric message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criterion listed: Appropriateness of visual images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall vocal delivery (evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess vocal performance including clarity, tone, comedic timing, and expressiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criterion listed: Overall vocal delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall physical delivery (evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess physical performance including gestures, posture, facial expression, and stage presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criterion listed: Overall physical delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice and rehearsal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rehearse the script with visuals to refine timing, delivery, and integration of media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing: Practice your presentation with your PowerPoint presentation so that it fits within a three- to five-minute broadcast segment. Schedule includes revising/rehearsing and final rehearsal/presentation dates.
